applies_why: The judge text treats [CR2] G as answering the rows and does not count any cited verse as an unanswered witness, so the K-G4 quote-and-name requirement is not triggered.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.
room: the phrase 'A verse the judge says was answered is not counted' — I weighed whether 'G answers' means the rows are answered and not counted, or whether lack of a quoted pressed sentence makes a verse an unanswered witness; the text says answered.
why: Because the text says the rows were answered rather than counting an unanswered witness, it does not do the thing K-G4 regulates.
